$comment: The NEXORA mesh on Google Cloud. This file is DATA, not a script: the plan is
read by `infra/gcp/plan.ts` (which validates it against the code that actually
exists) and applied by `infra/gcp/deploy.ts` (which shells out to gcloud).
Why a plan and not a shell script: a shell script that shells out to gcloud can
only be checked by running it, against a real project, with real credentials.
A plan can be checked against the source tree — that every service named here
exists, that every peer URL points at a service in this file, that every secret
a service refuses to boot without is mapped, that no secret value is written
down here. Those checks are the ones that catch drift, and drift is what breaks
a deployment at 2am.
The topology, and why each piece is what it is:
- Five Cloud Run services, one per service in the mesh. Independent deploys,
independent scaling, independent restarts. The code needs no change: every
service already reads its peers' URLs from the environment, and the gateway
already reads the same names.
- The gateway is the only one with a public ingress. The other four are
`internal`, which on Cloud Run means reachable only by other Cloud Run
services and the load balancer — not by the internet.
- The peer URLs are resolved in a second pass. A Cloud Run URL carries a hash
(`nexora-auth-abc123.run.app`) that is not known before the service exists,
so the deploy deploys the independents first, reads each URL back from the
API, and then deploys the dependents with those URLs filled in. The plan
says `{{auth}}` where the URL goes; the deploy fills it.
- Postgres is Cloud SQL, one instance, two databases (`authdb`, `billingdb`)
— one per service that owns data, so neither can read the other's tables
without asking.
- Secrets are Secret Manager. The plan names the Secret Manager entry and the
environment variable it lands in; the value is never in this file and never
in the image.
- The run receipts are signed by a key that lives in ONE service's
environment and nowhere else. The plan keeps that true:
`RECEIPT_ED25519_KEY` is mapped for `execution` only, because it is the
only service that runs code and signs what it observed, and the PUBLIC
half is what `auth` gets, because `auth` stores receipts and must not be
able to mint one.

services.name: nexora-curriculum
services.why: The roadmap and the phase bodies are read from disk and change rarely, so this scales to zero between lessons and costs nothing while idle. A cold start is a second of latency on a request a learner makes once.

services.name: nexora-billing
services.why: Billing is small, but a scale-to-zero here would put a cold start in front of a checkout — the one moment a learner is deciding whether to pay.

services.name: nexora-auth
services.why: Every authenticated request checks the revocation list, and the auth service is on that path, so it stays warm. Two instances because the gateway calls it on every request; a single instance is a single point of failure for the whole product.

services.name: nexora-execution

optionalEnv.EXECUTION_ALLOW_SUBPROCESS: Only consulted when EXECUTION_RUNNER is `subprocess`. This deployment uses the `docker` tier, and leaving this unset is exactly what keeps the subprocess tier refused at boot in production — a submitted program must not be able to read this service's own environment.
optionalEnv.EXECUTION_GO_CACHE: A path to a persistent Go build cache. Cloud Run's filesystem is ephemeral, so a shared cache would not survive a cold start; the runner image already carries a prewarmed standard-library cache, which is the part that costs every learner the most.
optionalEnv.NEXORA_TAKEHOME_PROJECT: Only read by the take-home path, where the acceptance suite is handed the learner's project root through the environment. The attested path judges against the platform's own canonical suites and never reads it.

services.why: The queue and the daily quota counters live in this process, so it must never scale to zero: a cold start would lose the jobs that were queued and reset the count of the day. Its concurrency is lower because each job is a container, not a request.

services.name: nexora-gateway

optionalEnv.CLERK_SECRET_KEY: Only read in clerk mode. This deployment runs AUTH_MODE=local, where the auth service signs its own tokens; switching to Clerk means setting this and re-running the plan check.
optionalEnv.CLERK_JWT_KEY: Only read in clerk mode, and only as the alternative to CLERK_SECRET_KEY. Local mode never fetches a JWKS, so there is no address to reach.
optionalEnv.CLERK_API_URL: Only read in clerk mode, and only to point at a self-hosted or sovereign Clerk instead of Clerk's hosted default. Local mode has no Clerk to point at.
optionalEnv.CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES: Only read in clerk mode. In local mode the allowed origin comes from FRONTEND_URL, which this plan sets.

services.why: The only public surface. Two instances so a deploy or a crash is not an outage, and the per-instance rate limit is the reason the second instance waits for a shared store (see OPERATIONS.md).

secrets.name: nexora-internal-api-key
secrets.purpose: Authenticates every service-to-service call. Derived from it is the key that signs run receipts, so a leaked one would let a caller mint receipts.

secrets.name: nexora-auth-jwt-secret
secrets.purpose: Signs the access tokens the gateway verifies without asking anyone.

secrets.name: nexora-receipt-ed25519-key
secrets.purpose: The operator-held Ed25519 receipt key. Its public half is published at GET /api/execute/verify-key so a stranger can re-derive a verdict offline.

secrets.name: nexora-receipt-ed25519-public-key
secrets.purpose: The PUBLIC half of the receipt key, for the auth service, which verifies receipts when they are synced and never mints one. The value is not secret — it is published at GET /api/execute/verify-key — but it is kept in Secret Manager so the two halves are versioned from one place, and so a rotation is one write rather than two.

secrets.name: nexora-resend-api-key
secrets.purpose: Transactional mail: password reset and email verification. Without it the requests still succeed and no mail is sent.

secrets.name: nexora-dodo-api-key
secrets.purpose: Dodo Payments API key. Without it checkout 503s and plan reads still work.

secrets.name: nexora-dodo-webhook-secret
secrets.purpose: Dodo's Standard-Webhooks signing secret, for verifying that a webhook really came from Dodo.

secrets.name: nexora-db-password
secrets.purpose: The Cloud SQL password for the `nexora` role. Written into the DATABASE_URL of the two services that own data.
